# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 44 (Bu-Vb Pc44)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc44
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 44
**Title (English, from literature):** Sitting with a woman in a concealed place
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rahopaṭicchanna-sikkhāpada* constitutes the forty-fourth *pācittiya* training rule in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. According to the rule, a Buddhist monk incurs an offense requiring confession if he sits down together with a woman in a secluded, concealed place seeking privacy [Hüsken 1997]. In the rule’s non-offense clauses (*anāpatti*), remaining standing rather than sitting is explicitly recognized as a ground for exemption, meaning that a monk standing with a woman in a secluded location does not contravene this particular regulation [Hüsken 1997].

 Equivalent counter-regulations exist for the nuns' community (*bhikkhunī* lineage), such as Pali *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya* 125, which regulates analogous seclusion with a man [Hüsken 1997].
